---
title: "Quarto Example: A Report Built at Render Time"
author: "Victor van Pelt"
format:
  beamer:
    theme: Madrid
    fontsize: 9pt
---

```{r}
#| include: false

# Use CRAN mirror (needed when running via Rscript / make / quarto)
options(repos = c(CRAN = "https://cloud.r-project.org"))

# Move to the project root whether we render from the root or from 1_code.
# knitr resets the working directory after every chunk, so we store ROOT and
# build absolute paths with file.path(ROOT, ...) instead of relying on setwd().
if (dir.exists(file.path(getwd(), "1_code"))) setwd(file.path(getwd(), "1_code"))
setwd("..")
ROOT <- getwd()

need <- c("sandwich", "tibble", "modelsummary")
to_install <- setdiff(need, rownames(installed.packages()))
if (length(to_install)) install.packages(to_install)  # repos taken from options()
invisible(lapply(need, require, character.only = TRUE))

# One self-contained pipeline: import -> transform -> analyse (no other file needed)
df <- read.csv(file.path(ROOT, "0_data", "gen_ai_earnings.csv"))
df$earnings_scaled <- df$earnings / 10
df <- df[df$earnings_scaled >= 0, , drop = FALSE]

mod <- lm(earnings_scaled ~ gen_ai, data = df)
vc  <- sandwich::vcovHC(mod, type = "HC1")           # robust SE, matches Stata's ", r"
```

## Table 1

```{r}
#| echo: false

# Robust Wald F for the single slope, computed from the same robust vcov the
# table uses. modelsummary's goodness-of-fit list for lm carries no F or p, so
# these rows are added explicitly; without them the table would silently omit
# both and stop matching the tables code.r and code.do write to 3_output.
b_q  <- coef(mod)
se_q <- sqrt(diag(vc))
n_q  <- as.integer(nobs(mod))
df_m <- length(b_q) - 1L  # model df (number of regressors)
F_q  <- unname((b_q["gen_ai"] / se_q["gen_ai"])^2)
p_q  <- pf(F_q, df_m, n_q - length(b_q), lower.tail = FALSE)

f3 <- function(x) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = 3)

gof_map <- data.frame(
  raw   = c("nobs", "r.squared"),
  clean = c("Observations", "$R^2$"),
  fmt   = c(0, 3)
)

add_rows_tbl <- tibble::tibble(
  term      = c("F", "p-value"),
  `Model 1` = c(f3(F_q), f3(p_q))
)

# coef_map fixes the row order and renames the intercept, so this table lists
# the same rows, in the same order, as the ones code.r and code.do write.
# escape = FALSE lets the $R^2$ label reach LaTeX as maths.
modelsummary::modelsummary(
  list("Model 1" = mod),
  vcov      = list(vc),
  statistic = "({std.error})",
  stars     = c("*" = .10, "**" = .05, "***" = .01),
  coef_map  = c("gen_ai" = "gen\\_ai", "(Intercept)" = "Constant"),
  gof_map   = gof_map,
  add_rows  = add_rows_tbl,
  escape    = FALSE,
  fmt       = 3,
  title     = "TABLE 1 - REGRESSIONS OF SCALED EARNINGS ON GENERATIVE AI",
  notes     = "Robust standard errors in parentheses. * p < 0.10, ** p < 0.05, *** p < 0.01.",
  output    = "latex"   # emit LaTeX into the slide; no .tex file created
)
```
